bullets: Macro is risk management at scale — the core job is avoiding the wrong side of a regime change rather than predicting every move correctly.
A regime change named in advance is one that can be positioned for; anything short of that is just hoping.
The economy is a system, not a set of levers — pulling one lever moves three others, so interventions never act in isolation.
Back-tested calls showed misses consistently came from treating a correlated system as if its parts were independent.
A macro book and a power grid are both systems of correlated risk, making macro analysis and sustainability work the same discipline under different vocabulary.
Systems thinking and risk management are one discipline rather than two — the underlying logic of correlated risk carries across domains.
